title: Boolean Indexing in Pandas - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Boolean indexing is a filtering technique in Pandas that selects rows or columns based on boolean conditions (True or False). Instead of using row labels or integer positions, it retrieves data by evaluating conditions on column values or index values.

  • Accessing a DataFrame with a boolean index
  • Applying a boolean mask to a dataframe
  • Masking data based on column value
  • Masking data based on an index value

Example: Filter Rows Based on a Condition

Python 
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "name": ["Aparna", "Pankaj", "Sudhir", "Geeku"],
    "score": [90, 40, 80, 98]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
print(df[df["score"] > 80])

Output
     name  score
0  Aparna     90
3   Geeku     98

Filtering Data Using Comparison Operators

Boolean indexing can be performed using comparison operators such as ==, !=, >, <, >=, and <=..

Python 
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "name": ["Aparna", "Pankaj", "Sudhir", "Geeku"],
    "degree": ["BCA", "BCA", "M.Tech", "BCA"],
    "score": [90, 40, 80, 98]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
print(df[df["degree"] == "BCA"])

Output
     name degree  score
0  Aparna    BCA     90
1  Pankaj    BCA     40
3   Geeku    BCA     98

Explanation:

  • df["degree"] == "BCA" creates a boolean Series.
  • df[...] returns rows where the condition is True.

Using Multiple Conditions

Multiple conditions can be combined using logical operators such as & (AND), | (OR), and ~ (NOT).

Python 
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "name": ["Aparna", "Pankaj", "Sudhir", "Geeku"],
    "degree": ["MBA", "BCA", "M.Tech", "MBA"],
    "score": [90, 40, 80, 98]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

print(
    df[
        (df["degree"] == "MBA")
        & (df["score"] > 90)
    ]
)

Output
    name degree  score
3  Geeku    MBA     98

Explanation:

  • & combines multiple conditions.
  • Parentheses are required around each condition.
  • Only rows satisfying both conditions are returned.

Using .loc[] with Boolean Conditions

.loc[] can be combined with boolean conditions to create more readable filtering operations.

Python 
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "name": ["Aparna", "Pankaj", "Sudhir", "Geeku"],
    "score": [90, 40, 80, 98]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

print(
    df.loc[
        df["score"] > 80
    ]
)

Output
     name  score
0  Aparna     90
3   Geeku     98

Explanation:

  • df["score"] > 80 creates a boolean Series.
  • .loc[] selects rows where the condition is True.

Filtering Using .isin()

.isin() checks whether values belong to a given list.

Python 
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "name": ["Aparna", "Pankaj", "Sudhir", "Geeku"],
    "degree": ["MBA", "BCA", "M.Tech", "MBA"]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

print(
    df[
        df["degree"].isin(
            ["MBA", "M.Tech"]
        )
    ]
)

Output
     name  degree
0  Aparna     MBA
2  Sudhir  M.Tech
3   Geeku     MBA

Explanation:

  • .isin() compares values against multiple options.
  • It returns a boolean Series used for filtering.

Filtering a Range of Values Using .between()

.between() filters rows whose values fall within a specified range.

Python 
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "score": [90, 40, 80, 98]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

print(
    df[
        df["score"].between(
            80,
            95
        )
    ]
)

Output
   score
0     90
2     80

Explanation:

  • .between(start, end) checks whether values lie within a range.
  • It returns a boolean Series for filtering.

Applying a Boolean Mask to a DataFrame

A boolean mask is a list or Series containing True and False values. Rows corresponding to True are selected.

Python 
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "name": ["Aparna", "Pankaj", "Sudhir", "Geeku"],
    "score": [90, 40, 80, 98]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

print(
    df[
        [True, False, True, False]
    ]
)

Output
     name  score
0  Aparna     90
2  Sudhir     80

Explanation:

  • The boolean list must have the same length as the DataFrame.
  • Rows corresponding to True are returned.

Filtering Based on Index Values

Boolean indexing can also filter rows using index values.

Python 
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "name": ["Aparna", "Pankaj", "Sudhir", "Geeku"]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
mask = df.index > 1
print(df[mask])

Output
     name
2  Sudhir
3   Geeku

Explanation:

  • df.index > 1 creates a boolean mask from index values.
  • df[mask] returns rows whose index is greater than 1.

Boolean Index Labels

Pandas also allows boolean values (True and False) to be used as row labels in the index.

Python 
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "name": ["Aparna", "Pankaj", "Sudhir", "Geeku"]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(
    data,
    index=[True, False, True, False]
)
print(df.loc[True])

Output
        name
True  Aparna
True  Sudhir

Explanation:

Boolean index labels are different from Boolean indexing. Instead of using True and False to filter rows based on conditions, the DataFrame itself uses boolean values as row labels in its index.

  • index=[True, False, True, False] creates a DataFrame whose row labels are boolean values.
  • df.loc[True] selects all rows whose index label is True.
  • Similarly, df.loc[False] selects all rows whose index label is False.
  • This technique is rarely used in practice and should not be confused with Boolean indexing, which filters rows using conditions.

Deprecated Methods

Some older Pandas methods related to indexing are deprecated and should not be used in modern code.

Example: The .ix[] indexer was a hybrid of .loc[] and .iloc[] that supported both label-based and integer-based indexing. It was deprecated in Pandas 0.20.0 and removed in Pandas 1.0 due to ambiguous behavior.

Avoid using:

df.ix[1]
df.ix["name"]

Use .loc[] for label-based indexing:

 df.loc[1]

Use .iloc[] for integer-based indexing:

df.iloc[1]

Indexing Methods

MethodPurpose
df.loc[]Label-based indexing
df.iloc[]Integer position-based indexing
df[]Column selection and boolean filtering
df.at[]Fast access to a single value by label
df.iat[]Fast access to a single value by integer position
